articles.title: A San Mamés a por el repóker
articles.standfirst: Matarazzo logra por primera vez en LaLiga cuatro triunfos seguidos, su tope también en la Bundesliga, y el domingo buscará en Bilbao la mejor marca de su carrera
articles.summary: Matarazzo logra por primera vez en LaLiga cuatro triunfos seguidos, su tope también en la Bundesliga, y el domingo buscará en Bilbao la mejor marca de su carrera
articles.body: Con la lograda contra el Levante Pellegrino Matarazzó alcanzó por primera vez en LaLiga cuatro victorias seguidas, después de que la pasada temporada se quedase en tres, una marca que intentará mejorar el próximo domingo frente al Athletic de Bilbao en San Mamés. Ni que decir tiene que sumar los tres puntos sería la mejor ratificación al gran momento que viven el equipo txuriurdin y su técnico, que enlazaría por primera vez en su carrera el repóker de triunfos consecutivos.. Matarazzo tuvo hace poco más de una decena de meses un gran impacto en la Real y en LaLiga, al llegar con el equipo tan sólo dos puntos por encima de los puestos de descenso y con unas muy malas sensaciones que enseguida convirtió en buenas, al enlazar seis jornadas sin perder, entre ellas tres triunfos consecutivos ante Getafe, Barcelona y Celta. Después su trayectoria se normalizó más, alternando victorias, empates y derrotas, hasta que logró el pase a la final de la Copa, ansiada por ser esta vez con público en la grada, no como la anterior de 2021, y esa decisiva cita y el título logrado en ella, con clasificación incluida para la Europa League, el otro objetivo del curso, hizo que la recta final ya poco importase. LaLiga 2026-27 arrancó con las dos conocidas visitas a Betis y Real Madrid, comprobando que el triunfo era muy complicado de lograr, aunque en La Cartuja estuvo cerca, pero luego ha aprovechado una fase menos dura de calendario para hacerse con seis victorias en ocho jornadas, las cuatro últimas seguidas, una mejor racha que puede ampliar el domingo en San Mamés con otro éxito que sería muy valioso a todos los niveles. Ganar en Bilbao permitiría a Matarazzo lograr su mejor marca de triunfos seguidos en su carrera como entrenador, ya que en sus distintas experiencias en la Bundesliga también llegó a cuatro, en la 2023-24 con el Hoffenheim, cuando superó a Heidenheim, Wolfsburgo, Colonia y Unión Berlín. El de Nueva Jersey tiene, por tanto, una motivación más para este derbi.

articles.title: Maxi López se moja sobre Julián: "Yo lo tuve de entrenador al Cholo. Y yo me voy al Barcelona..."
articles.standfirst: El exdelantero argentino considera que el fútbol azulgrana potenciaría al atacante del Atlético y apunta a unas promesas incumplidas por la dirigencia rojiblanca
articles.summary: El exdelantero argentino considera que el fútbol azulgrana potenciaría al atacante del Atlético y apunta a unas promesas incumplidas por la dirigencia rojiblanca
articles.body: Maxi López tiene claro dónde le habría gustado ver a Julián Álvarez este verano. El exdelantero argentino eligió el Barcelona y explicó su preferencia desde la experiencia de quien también estuvo a las órdenes de Diego Simeone. "Yo lo tuve de entrenador al Cholo. Y yo me voy al Barcelona...", aseguró en TyC Sports al analizar la situación del atacante del Atlético de Madrid. El futuro de Julián agitó el verano. Sus declaraciones durante el Mundial con Argentina abrieron un capítulo que terminó con su regreso al conjunto rojiblanco, donde continúa bajo las órdenes de Simeone. Desde Argentina, Maxi defendió los motivos del delantero para buscar una salida y sostuvo que otro destino habría favorecido su crecimiento. "Es el 9 de la selección argentina, por eso me hubiera gustado verlo en el Barcelona. Para mí el Barça juega mejor que el Atlético. Sinceramente, me hubiera gustado verlo en otro equipo este verano, porque lo potenciaría más. En su momento buscó salir del City para poder buscar minutos, porque tenía al lado al otro marciano. Y no tenía espacio. Fue al Atleti y encontró minutos. Después hubo una charla con la dirigencia, se dijeron cosas y le prometieron algo que después no se cumplió. Eso pasa siempre...", admitió López. Su argumento gira alrededor del juego y de las posibilidades de Julián para dar otro paso en su carrera. "Me hubiese gustado verlo en el Barcelona porque es el 9 de la selección argentina. Estaría en otro nivel", afirmó. El exjugador azulgrana llevó la comparación al terreno personal: "Yo estoy diciendo una cuestión mía personal. Y lo que veo a Julián como proyección". Maxi también puso en valor la transformación del Atlético desde la llegada del técnico argentino. "Me parece que lo que hizo el Cholo con el Atleti es para sacarse el sombrero, porque cuando yo llegué a España, el Atlético no peleaba nada. Él lo reconvirtió. Pero para el juego de Julián, me voy a un equipo que juegue mejor, y para mí el Barcelona juega mejor", sentenció. López conoce a Simeone de su etapa en el Catania, donde coincidieron como jugador y entrenador en 2011. El Cholo daba sus primeros pasos en los banquillos y Maxi había encontrado acomodo en el fútbol italiano después de un recorrido que le había llevado de River Plate al Barcelona.

articles.title: Major Chinese brands drop Mbappé as backlash grows over Mao joke
articles.summary: He allegedly said his "favourite meme" is "the one where they put my face on a Chinese dictator".
articles.body:
Several Chinese brands have dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé as backlash grew online over alleged comments by him referring to the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Mbappé reportedly told French talk show The Bridge a meme "that makes me laugh the most...the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator". As he speaks, a meme appears with his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

"I use it with my friends all the time," the Real Madrid forward adds, in unverified clips that have been circulating online.

Mbappé does not identify Mao by name and the original video is no longer on the show's YouTube channel, but screengrabs have spread on Chinese social media.

Even China's foreign ministry has weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

Neither Mbappé nor the The Bridge have commented on this yet.

It's unclear when the interview was broadcast but Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments on Monday night in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

"As his remarks were offensive to China and the Chinese people, we are unable to translate them," Dongqiudi added in its statement.

A backlash quickly ensued online, with some users criticising Mbappé – who is very popular in China and has huge brand endorsements – of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public".

"International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," read another comment on Weibo.

Mao founded Communist China in 1949 and ruled through tumultuous decades in the 1960s and 1970s. His attempt at rapid industrialisation, which he called the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party.

His death in 1976 brought a new era for China, which began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao's rule, he continued to be hailed by the Chinese Communist Party as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach.

The backlash against Mbappé is still growing. Chinese state broadcaster, CCTV, is suspending La Liga matches, Chinese media outlet The Paper reported on Tuesday.

According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, CCTV's news apps no longer have content related to the French striker.

The Chinese brands have not explicitly said why they were terminating the contract but referred to hurt sentiments.

The country's largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people".

Drinks giant Dongpeng, said: "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments."

Given brands have not mentioned the controversial clip, some users on social media are also asking what exactly Mbappé had said or done that was offensive.

Mbappé, who made his debut for Real Madrid in August 2024, has been nicknamed "the dictator" in the football world because of his influence and control over club and international football operations.

In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop's sandwiches. Some say the incident reinforced his "dictator" portrayal.

The nickname has also made Mbappé the subject of many memes online.

France team-mate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup by calling Mbappé Mobut – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades.

In an interview with France Football in September, Mbappé acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they "sometimes reveals a lack of political and human awareness among people".

"There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history.

"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life," he had said.

Additional reporting by Fan Wang and Osmond Chia

articles.title: Benítez señala el camino a Lamine con el ejemplo de Gordon: "Siempre sacará alguna cosa positiva"
articles.standfirst: El técnico recordó en Movistar las ganas de aprender del inglés y elogió la capacidad de Luis de la Fuente para adaptarse a sus jugadores
articles.summary: El técnico recordó en Movistar las ganas de aprender del inglés y elogió la capacidad de Luis de la Fuente para adaptarse a sus jugadores
articles.body: Rafa Benítez recurrió a una experiencia propia para explicar cuánto puede crecer todavía Lamine Yamal. En la alfombra roja de la Gala del Balón de Oro 2026, celebrada este lunes en Londres, el técnico español puso el ejemplo de Anthony Gordon, al que entrenó y que ahora comparte vestuario con el extremo en el Barcelona. Para Benítez, el margen de mejora empieza por la disposición a aprender: "La cuestión siempre es la mentalidad". Preguntado por Maldini en Movistar sobre el potencial del '10' azulgrana, incluso ante un posible cambio de posición, Benítez destacó el recorrido que tiene por delante. "A ver, todos los jugadores siempre decimos, 'he aprendido mucho de este entrenador' o he aprendido una cosa de este entrenador. Claro, él tiene mucho recorrido todavía y aprenderá, seguro". El recuerdo de Gordon le sirvió para desarrollar esa idea. "En mi experiencia como entrenador, los jugadores que progresan... yo he tenido a Anthony Gordon, y ya lo he explicado en alguna ocasión y creo que lo habéis escuchado. Anthony era un chaval que quería mejorar, y él hablaba con nosotros y practicaba su español y quería mejorar. Entonces ha mejorado y seguirá mejorando porque él escucha. Entonces los jugadores tienen que escuchar y aunque sea el peor entrenador del mundo, siempre vas a sacar una cosa positiva, eso es lo que tienen que pensar". Benítez también elogió a Luis de la Fuente y el fútbol de la selección española, reciente campeona del Mundial. "Disfruto viendo a España. Evidentemente está jugando muy bien, o sea, a cualquiera que le guste el fútbol le gusta el juego de la selección". El entrenador recordó una conversación con el seleccionador durante el Europeo para explicar qué valora de su trabajo: la capacidad para aprovechar las características de sus futbolistas. "Además, yo que estuve en el europeo y estuve charlando con él, cuando se gana y demás, lo que me gusta es que no juegan... 'es que tenemos que tener posesión'. Dice, yo tengo jugadores rápidos en las bandas y desequilibrantes, pues juego rápido a las bandas. Es que tengo velocidad en el contraataque, juego contraataque, y si juegas a tener la posesión, tienes a Pedri y a Rodrigo, pues juegas a posesión. Yo creo que lo bueno y lo inteligente que está haciendo Luis es adaptarse mucho dentro de una manera de jugar a los jugadores que tiene, a la calidad de los jugadores que tiene". Encargado de entregar los premios al mejor entrenador masculino y femenino, Benítez aseguró que desconocía los nombres de los ganadores. También bromeó con la posibilidad de anunciar al seleccionador español al abrir el sobre: "Yo diré Luis y después me callaré, a ver qué pasa". Antes de la intervención de Benítez, Álvaro Benito había situado la mentalidad en el centro de otra reflexión sobre Lamine. El comentarista apuntó a la exigencia que supone sostener una carrera en la élite durante más de una década y recurrió a los dos futbolistas que marcaron ese listón. "Si tiene la mitad de mentalidad que Cristiano, vamos a ver una auténtica salvajada de carrera, pero lo que dice Gerard, lo más difícil es ser longevo y mantenerte en el estatus de número uno mundial durante 10, 12, 15 temporadas. Hay que tener la mentalidad de Leo y de Cristiano, que es muy difícil tenerla".

articles.title: Joan Laporta backs Hansi Flick after Barcelona’s El Clasico defeat: ‘It was a tough blow, but…’
articles.summary: Joan Laporta has backed Hansi Flick to lead Barcelona forward after the club’s 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in El Clasico, insisting that the team’s ambitions f...
articles.body:
Joan Laporta has backed Hansi Flick to lead Barcelona forward after the club's 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in El Clasico , insisting that the team's ambitions for the season remain unchanged.

Speaking at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium, the Barcelona president acknowledged the disappointment of losing to their rivals but pointed to the team's position at the top of La Liga.

Laporta attended the ceremony alongside UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin, where he also discussed Barcelona's response to the defeat and expressed confidence in Flick's leadership.

Laporta insists Barcelona remain on track after El Clasico defeat

Barcelona were unable to produce their usual performance against Real Madrid, suffering a 2-1 league defeat that dealt a setback to Flick's side.

However, Laporta believes the team's young squad can recover quickly and remain focused on its objectives.

"It was a tough blow, but the players are young and they bounce back quickly. We weren't able to play our usual game, but we're still top of the table.

Laporta is optimistic even after losing El Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"We're still top of La Liga and our expectations remain intact. And Flick is the ideal manager for Barça," he said, as per Mundo Deportivo .

Lamine Yamal finishes third in Ballon d'Or rankings

It must be noted that Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal finished third in the Ballon d'Or standings , behind Kylian Mbappé, while Rodri Hernández placed fourth.

Yamal's podium finish provided another individual milestone for the young Barcelona star, even as the club sought to move on from its defeat to Real Madrid.

Despite the Ballon d'Or disappointment, Lamine was awarded the well-deserved Kopa Trophy .

Joan Garcia reflects on Barcelona journey at Ballon d'Or gala

Meanwhile, Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia, who was nominated for Goalkeeper of the Year, also spoke at the ceremony and praised fellow nominees Unai Simon and David Raya.

"I'm very happy to be here, and I'm glad Unai Simon and David Raya are here too. The three of us are similar yet different.

"We all deserve to be here," he remarked.

Reflecting on his progress since joining Barcelona less than a year and a half earlier, Garcia added

"I've taken it in my stride. The people around you are very important. Looking back, I'm proud of how everything has gone."

Crucially, Laporta and Garcia made their comments before Harry Kane was announced as the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner.

articles.title: Barcelona president Joan Laporta admits Real Madrid Clasico defeat was ‘very tough’
articles.summary: Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou. This has helped Jose Mourinho’s team change the outlook of the title race.Los Blanc...
articles.body:
Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou . This has helped Jose Mourinho's team change the outlook of the title race.

Los Blancos travelled to the Spotify Camp Nou six points behind their Catalan rivals. They delivered a statement performance to cut that deficit in half.

Barcelona president Joan Laporta has now admitted that the result understandably left the team disappointed.

Laporta admits Barcelona are hurting after Clasico defeat

While attending Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, the Catalan club's president admitted that the defeat had been particularly painful.

"I won't lie to you, losing the Clasico was very tough," Laporta said, acknowledging the disappointment of losing to Madrid at home (h/t RM4Arab ).

Barcelona had entered Sunday's encounter with a perfect record in La Liga , winning all nine of their opening matches.

Real Madrid outplayed Barcelona in the Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Mourinho's side disrupted that momentum, with Kylian Mbappe scoring twice, the second time late in the game, to seal the victory.

Raphinha had briefly restored parity for Barcelona in the second half, but Jose Mourinho's tactics ensured Los Blancos returned with all three points.

Laporta also acknowledged that Barça had struggled to impose their usual style of play. However, he backed Hansi Flick and the team going forward.

Real Madrid deliver an important psychological blow

For Madrid, Laporta's words underline that Sunday's result goes beyond just three points in the league table.

Mourinho's team approached the contest with a resolute defensive structure . This limited Barça 's attacking opportunities.

Jose Mourinho will want his team to keep getting more consistent in the coming weeks. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The performance was arguably Madrid's best so far under Mourinho, and winning at the Camp Nou against a dominant Barça side is a sign of improvement for Los Blancos .

The victory might also have handed a psychological boost to the Catalan side, who were flying high before the start of the week.

Madrid should look to use this situation to push on and try to close the three-point gap if Barça drop any more points.

Barça clearly did not see what was coming from Jose Mourinho's men on Sunday, and it remains to be seen how the La Liga title race pans out from here.

articles.title: INDYCAR JUST DROPPED A 2027 SCHEDULE THAT COULD CHANGE EVERYTHING — BARCELONA, THE INDY 500 AND OVAL CHAOS!
articles.summary: IndyCar fans, start clearing your calendars. The 2027 schedule has arrived, and this could be one of the most exciting seasons the series has put together in...
articles.body:
IndyCar fans, start clearing your calendars. The 2027 schedule has arrived, and this could be one of the most exciting seasons the series has put together in years.

A historic trip to Barcelona. The greatest spectacle in racing. A return to Phoenix. Street fights, legendary road courses and a championship finale at Laguna Seca.

And the best part? Every IndyCar race will air on FOX in the United States for the third consecutive season.

This is the kind of calendar that deserves attention.

BARCELONA! INDYCAR IS GOING INTERNATIONAL! 🇪🇸

The biggest headline is the inaugural IndyCar race at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya on July 18.

The Spanish Grand Prix venue will host IndyCar for the first time, marking the series' first European race since 2007. It also gives five-time champion Alex Palou the opportunity to race an IndyCar in his home region.

Think about the possibilities. A new circuit for the series, an international audience and one of the sport's biggest stars racing close to home.

This is a genuine opportunity for IndyCar to expand its reach without abandoning the tracks that built its identity.

The 111th Indianapolis 500 takes place May 30, once again anchoring the month of May at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

The buildup includes the May 15 road-course race at IMS, followed by the biggest event on the IndyCar calendar.

There is nothing else quite like the Indianapolis 500. The history, the speed, the strategy and the unpredictability make it a centerpiece of American motorsports.

Now, combine that tradition with a schedule that takes the series from street circuits to high-speed ovals and international road racing.

OVAL FANS, YOU ARE GETTING A DOUBLEHEADER

The Milwaukee Mile returns for two races on Aug. 28-29.

The historic one-mile oval will give drivers two opportunities to collect crucial championship points during one weekend. With the season approaching its final stretch, that doubleheader could prove decisive.

Road America and Mid-Ohio also remain on the calendar, giving fans two very different road-course challenges.

The season concludes Sept. 5 at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. If the championship remains close, the Corkscrew could provide a dramatic setting for the finale.

IS INDYCAR FINALLY BUILDING THE CALENDAR FANS WANT?

No schedule is perfect, and losing stops in Nashville and Washington, D.C., will generate debate. But the 2027 lineup offers a compelling mix of tradition, variety and ambition.

The Indianapolis 500 remains the crown jewel. Milwaukee brings back a doubleheader. Arlington gets another chance to establish itself, and Barcelona gives the series an international showcase.

With every race returning to FOX, IndyCar also has a consistent broadcast platform to introduce new fans to the sport.

Now comes the hard part: turning a great-looking schedule into packed grandstands, memorable finishes and sustained momentum.

IndyCar fans, be honest: Is this one of the best schedules the series has put together in years? And does the Barcelona race have you more excited than ever for 2027?

articles.title: Alejandro Elorriaga, el médico español al que Kane dedicó el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: Llevan juntos desde marzo de 2020, cuando una grave lesión muscular marcó un punto de inflexión en la carrera del goleador del Bayern
articles.summary: El delantero inglés se ha acordado de su doctor deportivo al recoger el Balón de Oro. Llevan juntos desde marzo de 2020, cuando una grave lesión muscular marcó un punto de inflexión en la carrera del goleador del Bayern
articles.body: Hay nombres que rara vez aparecen en las portadas, pero que forman parte de la historia de los grandes deportistas. Alejandro Elorriaga Claraco es uno de ellos. Madrileño, médico deportivo y afincado desde hace décadas en Canadá, se ha convertido en una figura fundamental para Harry Kane. Tanto es así que el delantero inglés ha querido acordarse de él en el momento más importante de su carrera: la recogida del Balón de Oro. La relación entre ambos comenzó en marzo de 2020. Kane atravesaba entonces un momento complicado después de sufrir una rotura completa del tendón proximal del bíceps femoral izquierdo durante un partido el 1 de enero de aquel año. La lesión requirió una intervención quirúrgica y obligó al delantero a detenerse cuando todavía defendía los colores del Tottenham. Fue en ese contexto cuando entró en escena Elorriaga, un profesional que ha desarrollado buena parte de su trayectoria lejos de los focos del fútbol europeo. Desde entonces, el médico madrileño ha acompañado al internacional inglés en su preparación y recuperación, con un trabajo individualizado orientado a mejorar su estado físico y ayudarle a soportar las exigencias de la alta competición. Una relación construida durante más de seis años y medio que el propio futbolista ha reivindicado públicamente. "Alejandro ha desempeñado un papel muy importante en mi éxito", reconoció Kane en una entrevista concedida a MARCA en septiembre. El delantero fue todavía más explícito al explicar la importancia de esa colaboración. "Trabajamos mucho en la sombra", aseguró. Kane considera que Elorriaga es una de las principales razones por las que ha podido mantener su nivel, disputar tantos partidos y seguir mejorando con el paso de los años. Una afirmación especialmente significativa en un futbolista que ha firmado los mejores registros goleadores de su carrera durante su etapa en el Bayern de Múnich. Pero, ¿quién es el hombre al que Kane ha querido dar las gracias ante el mundo del fútbol?. Elorriaga dirige desde 1998 el programa Contemporary Medical Acupuncture de la Universidad McMaster, en Canadá, donde también ejerce como profesor clínico en el departamento de Anestesia. Su trayectoria está vinculada al tratamiento del dolor y a la recuperación funcional, con especial atención a las necesidades de los deportistas de alto rendimiento. Su perfil responde al de un especialista que prefiere el trabajo diario a la exposición pública. Su nombre ha ido ganando notoriedad a medida que se conocía su relación con Kane y la importancia que el propio jugador concede a su preparación física. En un fútbol cada vez más exigente, donde los calendarios apenas conceden tregua y cada ausencia puede alterar los planes de un equipo, la continuidad se ha convertido en un valor especialmente apreciado. Los números de Kane ayudan a entender el alcance de su reconocimiento. El inglés cerró la temporada 2025-26 con 73 goles en 65 partidos entre el Bayern y la selección inglesa, en el mejor curso de su carrera. Detrás de semejante producción hay talento, trabajo, compañeros y un equipo que le permite brillar. También, según sus propias palabras, profesionales como Alejandro Elorriaga, cuya aportación no siempre se ve cuando el delantero celebra un gol. El Balón de Oro tiene un ganador sobre el escenario, pero el reconocimiento de Kane recuerda que el rendimiento de una estrella no se construye únicamente durante los 90 minutos. A veces, una parte decisiva de la historia se escribe lejos del estadio, sin cámaras y sin aplausos. Elorriaga lleva años trabajando en ese lugar. Esta vez, sin embargo, su nombre también ha tenido su momento de protagonismo.

articles.title: Ezri Konsa: No William Saliba, no problem, as summer signing steps up for Arsenal
articles.summary: Arsenal's defensive form is testament to the performances of Ezri Konsa, who has stepped up in William Saliba's absence and been given his chance to shine.
articles.body:
When Arsenal confirmed in July that William Saliba would miss an "extended period" with a long-term back issue, you can forgive fans for panicking.

The Frenchman has formed a formidable pairing with Gabriel Magalhaes as part of the Gunners' well-drilled backline that conceded just 27 league goals last season as they lifted the Premier League title.

Eight games into the new season and Saliba still hasn't featured, but Mikel Arteta's side have conceded the fewest goals in the Premier League as they sit level on points at the summit.

That form is testament to the performances of Ezri Konsa, who has stepped up in Saliba's absence and been given his chance to shine.

Before Arsenal signed the 29-year-old for £55m from Aston Villa in August, questions were asked. Is it too much money? Do the Gunners need him with Cristhian Mosquera already in the squad? Why bring in Konsa and not a forward?

But now, the debate is whether Konsa and Gabriel are the best partnership in world football, not just the Premier League.

Arsenal already had seven senior defenders on the books when they signed Konsa.

And add in the fact they already had one of the most solid partnerships in world football too, it can be understood why there was confusion about such a big outlay.

Arsenal have changed their recruitment strategy, focusing on signings in the peak of their career as they look to capitalise on their win window and continue to lift silverware.

Konsa is exactly what they are looking for - in his prime.

The defender made 286 appearances for Villa after joining in July 2019 from Brentford and helped them win the Europa League in May, the club's first European trophy since 1982.

He has established himself as a first-choice starter for England and started seven of their eight games at the World Cup.

His former Aston Villa team-mate, Morgan Rogers - who himself made a big-money move this summer when he joined Chelsea for £117m - said at the World Cup that Konsa does not get the credit he deserves and that he is "one of the best centre-backs in football".

Konsa is an imposing figure, quick across the ground, and his aggression in challenges has impressed supporters.

Having signed on the opening day of the season, Arteta has praised the way the centre-back has settled in as "unbelievable".

"He's gone to a huge club like Arsenal with no pre-season when Saliba is here, with other players that are already here," Arteta added of Konsa's start.

"To position yourself in that manner, with that naturality I would say, and performing at the level that he's doing and building already a chemistry and a balance with Gabi that seems so solid, it's very difficult to do and we are really lucky to have him."

Individually, Konsa had the best pass-completion rate of any player in the Premier League last season and he tops the chart again this season with 96% success rate from his 324 passes.

He also ranked top for success rate among all Premier League outfielders to contest 20 or more ground duels during the last campaign and is currently ranked 12th for this in 2026-27.

Arsenal have kept a clean sheet in five of their eight games, with no team keeping more in the Premier League this season.

After joining just hours before their season-opener against Coventry , Konsa has started six of those matches, while he came on for his debut in their second match against former club Villa after Mosquera picked up an injury.

"The two of them [Saliba and Gabriel] were on the Ballon D'or list as the best defenders in world football," Former Arsenal defender Martin Keown said on Match of the Day.

"He has not been overshadowed at all by the people he has played alongside."

And Konsa produced another impressive performance when he scored his first goal for Arsenal against Everton on Saturday.

"I've come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It's not surprising to me," Konsa said of Arsenal 's strong start to the season.

"We are champions and to be champions you've got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible."

Gabriel and Konsa partnership is flourishing

Nine starts, seven wins, five clean sheets, two goals between them - the partnership of Konsa and Gabriel could not be going much better.

The pair both scored as the Gunners beat Everton and it was the first time that Arsenal had two centre-backs score in a Premier League match since February 2024, which coincidentally also came against a David Moyes team (Gabriel and Saliba against West Ham).

Konsa has also started all three of Arsenal 's games alongside Gabriel in the Champions League and the Gunners are unbeaten as the formidable partnership continues to flourish.

The England international has said that Gabriel made "my life easy since I've joined the club and it's been a pleasure playing alongside him".

Gabriel's regular partner Saliba still has no date for a return but is currently doing individual training work on grass.

When asked whether there is less pressure on Saliba rushing to get back, Arteta was keen to remind everyone of his quality.

"William is not fit and we are desperate to have him back because we know what he offers," he said.

"We are really lucky to have that and I'm sure when Mosquera plays that he will be the same because they have something special those boys.

"The way we train them, the way they want to improve as well and how they look after each other. That's the beauty of our team."

The next challenge for Konsa will be when Saliba returns.

But with his ability to play right-back too, he doesn't only have one route into the starting XI.

articles.title: ‘Our pride is in play’ - Mikel Arteta issues stern warning to Arsenal stars ahead of Fleetwood Town clash
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has sent a clear message to his Arsenal stars, warning them that their reputations are on the line ahead of Tuesday's Carabao Cup trip to Fleetw...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has sent a clear message to his Arsenal stars, warning them that their reputations are on the line ahead of Tuesday's Carabao Cup trip to Fleetwood. The Gunners boss is determined to avoid a repeat of the club's darkest cup moments as they prepare to face the lowest-ranked side left in the tournament.

Arsenal travel to League Two outfit Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night for a fourth-round Carabao Cup tie. The hosts are the lowest-ranked side still in the competition, currently sitting 18th in the fourth tier of English football.

With a crucial Premier League clash against Liverpool looming on the horizon, the Gunners are expected to field a heavily rotated starting line-up. However, Arteta expects maximum effort from whichever players cross the white line, demanding they show total respect to their underdog opponents.

The Arsenal manager insists his pre-match instructions will be incredibly brief. He wants his squad to showcase their quality immediately and leave no room for a giant-killing.

"Show them the Arsenal shirt and what we represent and that's it," Arteta told reporters. "We need to go there and win the game. That's it. It's very simple."

The Spaniard was quick to remind his players that their elite standards cannot drop simply because of the opposition's league standing.

He added: "Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that. Then try to win and try to play a bit better than them."

The Arsenal boss knows all too well the dangers of underestimating lower-league opposition. Back in 2012, Arteta was part of Arsene Wenger's squad that suffered a humiliating penalty shootout defeat to Bradford City in the quarter-finals of this very competition.

That infamous shock serves as a stark reminder of how quickly cup ties can unravel if the heavy favourites fail to apply themselves. The 44-year-old is using that painful memory to keep his current crop grounded in reality.

"We all had one at some stage and we know the risk," Arteta explained. "In football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things. That's when our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game."

Once Tuesday's cup commitments are fulfilled, Arsenal's immediate attention will shift to a massive Premier League showdown. The Gunners head to Anfield to face Liverpool this weekend, a fixture that arrives in the middle of a gruelling schedule.

Arteta must carefully balance his squad rotation at Fleetwood to ensure his key stars are fresh for the trip to Merseyside, without compromising their progression into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. Navigating this midweek tie efficiently will be critical to maintaining their momentum ahead of a season-defining domestic test.

articles.title: Chinese brands cut ties with French soccer star Mbappé over ‘Chinese dictator’ remark
articles.summary: BEIJING (AP) — French soccer star Kylian Mbappé's face appears in ads across China, from subway stations to elevators, but now at least three companies are c...
articles.body:
BEIJING (AP) — French soccer star Kylian Mbappé's face appears in ads across China, from subway stations to elevators, but now at least three companies are cutting ties with the national team captain after he made some comments apparently referring to Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China, as a dictator.

Beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy giant Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground announced Tuesday in similarly worded statements that they were ending agreements with the soccer star , each saying they oppose "any words and actions that hurt national sentiment."

The companies did not specify what prompted their decisions, but they released their statements after a clip that appeared to show Mbappé being interviewed ahead of going on the French online talk show "The Bridge" circulated on X.

In the video, Mbappé is asked about his favorite meme of himself, and the soccer star replies that it was "a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator" before the video shows an altered image depicting Mbappé's face on the blue-suited body of Mao Zedong.

Soccer fans online jokingly call the star — who's said to overshadow many of his teammates and even the teams he plays on — a dictator, and memes showing him as Mao or other autocratic leaders are widely circulated.

The Associated Press was immediately unable to reach Mbappé's representatives for comment.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said in response to a question about the controversy that "words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

Social media platform RedNote joined the criticism, saying in a separate statement that the company had a content partnership with Mbappé that ended on Dec. 31, 2024, and that it would "remove related promotional materials." It likewise expressed opposition to "any conduct that hurts national sentiment."

Mbappé's account on RedNote was not accepting new followers Tuesday.

Mbappé has featured in advertising campaigns in China for products from electrolyte drinks to milk and cheese. In one commercial for Dongpeng, Mbappé delivers a slogan in Chinese; in an ad for Mengniu, he appears alongside Argentine soccer star Lionel Messi.

On Chinese social media, there were already several comments criticizing the soccer star.

The hashtags "Dongpeng ends partnership with Mbappé" and "Several brands end partnerships with Mbappé" topped Weibo's trending list. "Football fans boycott Mbappé" was also trending, with some users expressing anger at his remarks or telling him not to come to China.

Associated Press video producer Olivia Zhang contributed to this report from Beijing.

The Dallas Cowboys delivered a ringing statement on Monday Night Football in Week 7, rolling past the rival Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 at Lincoln Financial Field. While running back Javonte Williams anchored the ground game with 155 rushing yards and a touchdown on 25 carries, the explosive receiving duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens stole the spotlight in prime time.

Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott threw for 212 passing yards and three touchdowns, directing a balanced offensive attack that kept Philadelphia off balance all evening. All three of Prescott's touchdown passes landed in the hands of his star wideouts. Lamb hauled in two scoring passes, including a key 16-yard touchdown catch late in the third quarter that put Dallas ahead for good. Pickens added an acrobatic 21-yard touchdown reception right before halftime to set the physical tone.

When reporters asked Lamb postgame how dangerous the Dallas Cowboys offense becomes when both wide receivers produce at a high level simultaneously, the star playmaker offered a fearless assessment of their group's ceiling.

Lamb's bold declaration comes as Dallas snaps a two-game skid to improve to 3-4 on the season. The offensive outbreak stood in stark contrast to the struggling Philadelphia Eagles, who fell to 2-5 after dropping their fifth consecutive contest. Philadelphia backup quarterback Tanner McKee threw for 211 yards and a touchdown in place of injured starter Jalen Hurts, while running back Saquon Barkley rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.

With Prescott operating efficiently and Williams establishing physical dominance on the ground, the dual threat of Lamb and Pickens provides Dallas with a lethal perimeter identity. If both pass-catchers stay locked in, opposing secondary units across the NFL will struggle to prove Lamb wrong.

articles.title: ‘Let’s Not Get Carried Away’ — Troy Aikman Not Putting Too Much Stock Into Cowboys’ MNF Win Over Hobbled Eagles
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys dominated the Philadelphia Eagles in a 38-21 Week 7 blowout on the road on Monday Night Football. The decimated Eagles could not withstand...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys dominated the Philadelphia Eagles in a 38-21 Week 7 blowout on the road on Monday Night Football. The decimated Eagles could not withstand the Cowboys' offensive firepower as coach Brian Schottenheimer's team finally put up a balanced performance on both sides of the ball.

While that win served to wash the bad taste out from the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers, Troy Aikman remains unconvinced this is a legitimate turning point for his beloved franchise.

Why Troy Aikman Is Unconvinced by Cowboys' Huge Week 7 Win

During the postgame broadcast, Aikman was asked by Scott Van Pelt whether the win changed his perspective on the Cowboys, and he answered in the negative.

"Eh, not really. Not really. And I don't mean that as a negative," Aikman said . "This is a beat-up Philadelphia team. To come in here and win tonight, I mean, let's not get carried away. They did what you kind of expected them to do. I did think the Eagles defensively would put up more of a fight than what they did. But it'll bear itself out as we move forward.

"This team's capable. Defense did some good things. They've still got a ways to go. But that's gonna be the key to this team, is how far along can this defense come between now and when the playoffs roll around, if they get in."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

There were still poorly timed penalties and blown coverages by the defense against the limited Eagles, but the return of linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who missed the Cowboys' last five games with a hamstring injury, proved a welcome relief for Christian Parker's unit.

That said, Dallas unfortunately still boasts the league's worst PFN Defense Impact score at 61.4.

The offense, led by quarterback Dak Prescott and wide receivers George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, shook off its lethargy and dominated the Eagles' defense. Dallas has earned a PFN Offense Impact score of 86.1 (No. 3 in the NFL).

The Cowboys have a favorable schedule in the coming weeks, starting with a home game against the Arizona Cardinals and a road game against the hapless Indianapolis Colts, giving them a chance to go on a winning run before a high-profile clash against the San Francisco 49ers.

Dallas has just four games remaining against teams projected to reach the playoffs, and Schottenheimer's team now has a chance to take control of the NFC East.

During his postgame news conference, Prescott, who amassed 212 passing yards and 3 touchdowns, emphasized the importance of momentum in the league and urged the team to take advantage of the win over the Eagles.

"Momentum's real," Prescott said. "Especially in this league, especially in what we do. Just understanding the parity and how tough this league is, when you get a win, the confidence it gives your group, the confidence it gives this team, and just being able to build off of that, and the benefit of also going home, having a couple of home games in a row, but only this week matters."

After finishing 7-9-1 last season, Dallas invested heavily in turning the team into a playoff contender and, with one of the league's best offenses, could be poised to reach the playoffs for the first time since 2023.

articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco celebra en La Tribu el triunfo de Harry Kane y critica tanto las entrevistas previas de los otros dos como su reacción al conocer al ganador
articles.body: La victoria de Harry Kane en el Balón de Oro ha provocado numerosas reacciones en el mundo del fútbol. Una de ellas ha sido la de David Sánchez, que en La Tribu de Radio MARCA ha celebrado el reconocimiento al delantero inglés y ha lanzado una dura crítica contra Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé por su actitud antes y después de la entrega del galardón. "Me alegro de que ganase el Balón de Oro Harry Kane. Y me alegro porque creo que se lo merece y porque hizo una temporada espectacular", ha comenzado señalando el periodista, que ha querido destacar especialmente la actitud del futbolista inglés durante las semanas previas a la ceremonia. "Y, además, me alegro porque Harry Kane no se ha arrastrado para pedir y mendigar un Balón de Oro que ya lo merecía de por sí", ha añadido David Sánchez, estableciendo así una comparación con los otros dos aspirantes al premio. El periodista considera que las declaraciones de los dos futbolistas en los días previos a la entrega del Balón de Oro pudieron generar rechazo entre algunos aficionados de sus propios equipos. "Tengo la sensación que una parte del madridismo y otra parte del barcelonismo no quería que ganase ese Balón de Oro ni Mbappé ni Lamine Yamal", ha asegurado. David Sánchez ha explicado también el motivo de esa percepción: "Porque a mucha gente le ha chirriado esa ronda de entrevistas lamentable de Lamine Yamal y de Mbappé mendigando un Balón de Oro". Sin embargo, las críticas del periodista no se han limitado a las declaraciones anteriores a la gala. "Y lo peor, la reacción de ambos al conocerse el ganador del Balón de Oro. Ni se levantaron ni felicitaron y todo fueron caritas serias hasta que abandonaron el recinto", ha lamentado. Para terminar, David Sánchez ha dejado una reflexión sobre la actitud que deben mostrar los futbolistas cuando no consiguen un reconocimiento individual: "Hay que saber ganar, pero, sobre todo, hay que saber perder". "Honores a Harry Kane, merecedor de este Balón de Oro", ha sentenciado el periodista en La Tribu de Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Value Adder: Luka Vuskovic to Liverpool is a Premier League bombshell
articles.summary: Liverpool could strike a Premier League bombshell by signing Luka Vuskovic. The Reds' interest is said to be serious.Liverpool are on the hunt for a new cent...
articles.body:
Liverpool could strike a Premier League bombshell by signing Luka Vuskovic. The Reds' interest is said to be serious.

Liverpool are on the hunt for a new centre-back and Luka Vuskovic is understandably a name that keeps popping up. The Croatian took the Bundesliga by storm last season, performing as one of the very best in the league at only 18.

That earned him a move to Brighton from Tottenham Hotspur. That doesn't admittedly sound like a jump up but the Seagulls were willing to give Vuskovic a starting role immediately - exactly what he needed at this stage.

His efforts with Hamburg shouldn't have led to a season on the sidelines. Vuskovic needed to carry on that momentum and he absolutely has, playing a big role in Brighton's superb start to the campaign.

That naturally has bigger clubs looking. Vuskovic wasn't necessarily going to get regular first-team football if he'd moved to Liverpool or Real Madrid last summer. But after a full Premier League season? Very possibly.

It means the likes of Teamtalk say that Liverpool, Real Madrid and Barcelona have serious interest. And we think it's got the potential to be a true bombshell signing for the Reds.

Vuskovic was one of the stories of last season as he took to an elite-level league in the Bundesliga like it was nothing. Our Value Adder data model ranked him as the 8th most valuable teenage player across the top five leagues.

But it's worth noting that he's the only defensive player in the top 8. In fact, the only defensive players in the top 10 are Vuskovic and Barcelona's Pau Cubarsi.

For purely defensive value, Vuskovic was in the top 10 for players under 24. Note that that's 'players': we're not just looking at centre-backs here.

Get rid of the age bracket and Vuskovic is 18th among all centre-backs. It's an outrageous position for a teenager - there are only two other players under 24 in the top 20, let alone 18.

Attacking value? Vuskovic is 6th across all centre-backs in the top five leagues and this is where we think the real bombshell is. There are very, very few centre-backs who can deliver at both ends.

Liverpool have had arguably the best at both for a long time now in Virgil van Dijk. The Dutchman sits just one place ahead of Vuskovic last season, finishing 5th for attacking value in centre-backs across the top five leagues.

The Reds' defence has been anchored by Van Dijk since 2018 and we do expect that time to come to an end next year. How incredible, then, that Liverpool may find his successor in Vuskovic.

How many other centre-backs can claim to be above the 95th percentile in their top 5 league for shots per 90, share of the defensive output, aerials won, defensive actions, and attacking actions? Now how many are doing that before turning 20?

Vuskovic is an outrageous talent and perhaps Liverpool's best chance of finding a genuine Van Dijk successor. Not just a good centre-back to replace him but the next generation's equivalent. A player so unique and so well-rounded that he's a thorn in the side of every other Premier League club.

Because that's the bombshell here. While every club has been waiting for Liverpool to finally be rid of Van Dijk, they may just go and get another one.

It has certainly been a testing few weeks for Manchester United and their fans.

This meant he finished "behind Dayot Upamecano and ahead of Julian Quinones, William Saliba and Sadio Mane."

It is the second time that he has been nominated for the award.

articles.title: Every Bundesliga Ballon d'Or winner, from Gerd Müller to Harry Kane
articles.summary: Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or, becoming the first Bundesliga-based player to claim football's most prestigious individual award since Matthias Samm...
articles.body:
Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or , becoming the first Bundesliga -based player to claim football's most prestigious individual award since Matthias Sammer in 1996.

The Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals for club and country during the 2025/26 campaign, capping a remarkable season with the game's biggest individual honour.

Kane is the seventh player to win the Ballon d'Or while playing for a Bundesliga club, joining a distinguished group that includes Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer and Kevin Keegan .

Gerd Muller became German football's first Ballon d'Or winner after winning the 1970 award. Der Bomber scored 38 league goals for Bayern Munich to win the European Golden Shoe, before adding 10 goals to win the Golden Boot as West Germany finished third at the 1970 World Cup.

Muller failed to win a team trophy, but beat Bobby Moore to the Ballon d'Or.

Franz Beckenbauer, Bayern Munich - 1972 and 1976

Franz Beckenbauer was the first German to win multiple Ballon d'Or trophies after success in 1972 and 1976.

Beckenbauer's first award came after West Germany won the 1972 European Championship, beating Soviet Union in the final. Beckenbauer had earlier led Bayern Munich to Bundesliga title success.

Four years later, Beckenbauer claimed a second Ballon d'Or. Der Kaiser was recognised after Bayern Munich secured a third consecutive European Cup. He was also Ballon d'Or runner-up in 1974 and 1975.

Allan Simonsen, Borussia Monchengladbach - 1977

Allan Simonsen remains Denmark's only Ballon d'Or winner, having succeeded Franz Beckenbauer to claim the award in 1977.

The forward starred for Borussia Mönchengladbach as the club won the Bundesliga title and reached the European Cup final, scoring against Liverpool in a 3-1 defeat. Simonsen remains the only player to have scored in the finals of the European Cup, UEFA Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup.

Kevin Keegan collected the Ballon d'Or in 1978 and 1979 and remains the only English footballer to have won multiple awards. Keegan moved to Hamburg in a record-breaking £500,000 deal in 1977, having helped Liverpool to European Cup success.

He won the Ballon d'Or in each of his first two seasons in Germany, after scoring 29 goals in 70 games. His second season saw Hamburg win the Bundesliga for the first time in 19 years.

Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Bayern Munich - 1980 and 1981

The Bundesliga's dominance of the Ballon d'Or continued into the early eighties, as Karl-Heinz Rummenigge's back-to-back wins made it six straight years with a German-based winner.

Rummenigge won the 1980 Ballon d'Or after scoring 36 goals in 47 games for Bayern Munich, before earning the Best Player Award as Germany won the 1980 European Championship.

A year later, he was the top scorer in the Bundesliga and European Cup to earn a second Ballon d'Or.

Matthias Sammer, Borussia Dortmund - 1996

Matthias Sammer became only the second defender to win the Ballon d'Or after winning the 1996 award.

Having had success in a sweeper role during Borussia Dortmund's Bundesliga title success, Sammer starred in a similar position for Germany at Euro '96. He helped the Germans to success, earning the Player of the Tournament prize and later the Ballon d'Or.

Harry Kane ended the Bundesliga's 30-year wait for a Ballon d'Or winner after winning the 2026 vote.

Kane scored 73 goals for club and country to win the award, scoring 61 times for Bayern Munich to inspire the club's German treble.

After picking up the European Golden Shoe , he struck six times at the 2026 World Cup as England finished third. That represented England's best ever World Cup performance in an overseas tournament.

articles.title: ‘Highly likely’ – Insider’s transfer claim on Ronald Araujo will be music to Liverpool fans’ ears

articles.body:
It's been claimed that Liverpool will 'already be working on' trying to turn the loan deal for Ronald Araujo into a permanent transfer in 2027.

The Uruguayan defender – who's contracted to Barcelona – is spending this season at Anfield and hasn't taken long to make a huge impression on the Merseyside natives.

He'd already been a darling of the Kop ever before his virtuoso performance in the 2-0 win over Brighton on Sunday, when he threw himself in front of the ball with whatever body part necessary in order to preserve the Reds' clean sheet.

Liverpool backed to sign Araujo permanently

Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown believes that Liverpool chiefs will have wasted no time in getting to work on a potential permanent transfer for Araujo, which he believes is quite likely to materialise.

He told Football Insider : "Liverpool will already be working on that deal to sign Araujo on a permanent deal. It's already happening.

"When you get a player like that on loan and he hits the ground running, the immediate inclination is to make sure you have everything lined up behind the scenes. That's what Liverpool will be doing now, because the manager has liked what he has seen from him so far, especially after that display against Brighton.

"They'll obviously keep a close eye on how he gets on for the rest of the season, and a decision will be made before the summer, but they want to have it lined up already.

"Araujo has been terrific. He's become a very important player for Liverpool, and if he continues to impress as he has been, then he is highly likely to stay permanently."

Permanent deal for Araujo seems like a no-brainer

It isn't just Liverpool fans who are imploring the club to sign Araujo permanently – journalist David Lynch has also stated that an outright move for the 27-year-old is a must.

There's an option to trigger a permanent transfer ( understood to be £47m ), and based on what we've seen from the Uruguayan so far, it seems like a no-brainer to exercise that and keep him at Anfield beyond next summer.

Whilst signed initially as centre-back cover at a time when depth in that position was theadbare, he has excelled at right-back so far this season, bringing settlement to an area which had been quite problematic and unstable for the Reds over the past year.

It's already been reported (via Marca ) that Liverpool are prepared to sign Araujo outright if his current performance levels remain consistent, and he's hardly put a foot wrong in a red shirt in his opening 12 appearances.

Whether that's a mere purple patch or a sign of things to come remains to be seen, but all the evidence so far would point to the Reds taking up the purchase option on the 27-year-old, which'd be music to the ears of Kopites who've taken an instant shine to him.

articles.title: La influencia de MARCA y la entrevista que decantó la balanza
articles.summary: La opinión del director
articles.body: Echo la vista atrás y me sitúo en el ecuador del plazo para votar al ganador del Balón de Oro. Ese decisivo momento en el que, tras lo conseguido sobre el césped, cualquier movimiento, declaración o estrategia aún podía tener efecto sobre los electores, que después se hicieron muchas inútiles componendas con las urnas ya cerradas y los sufragios ya emitidos. "Que Harry Kane salga en la portada de MARCA puede decantar la balanza", me comentó un veterano periodista europeo, buen conocedor de los entresijos de este galardón, cuando leyó en nuestra primera página la entrevista con el goleador inglés. En ese momento el debate estaba muy abierto, la pelea se antojaba reñidísima y, de forma inusual y bastante chocante los candidatos habían empezado a postularse, exageradamente, pidiendo el voto para sí mismos. Harry Kane decidió no tomar ese camino, tan legítimo como sorprendente. En su lugar usó un atajo mucho más efectivo: consciente de la influencia, la capacidad de prescripción y el alcance de MARCA, y atendiendo en este sentido la recomendación acertada y oportuna del Bayern de Múnich, eligió nuestro periódico para lanzar al mundo su mensaje. En la extensa y profunda entrevista concedida a Juan Castro en la capital bávara, Kane afirmó: "No me gusta hablar de mí, los 73 goles hablan por sí solos". Esa frase dio la vuelta al planeta. Con la portada aún caliente sobre la mesa, el plazo de elección abierto y las votaciones en plena ebullición, recibí ese mensaje premonitorio. "Sois muy influyentes, esta entrevista va a tener mucho impacto". ¿Qué hubiera pasado si algún otro candidato hubiera replicado la estrategia de Kane? No lo sé. Bueno, sí lo sé, pero eso ya es agua pasada. Más allá de preferencias personales o editoriales (especialmente en un año en el que España ha ganado el Mundial de fútbol o en el que nuestro flamante premio Pichichi también aspiraba al dorado galardón) resulta inamovible que Harry Kane es el meritorio propietario del Balón de Oro y su nombre queda desde anoche para siempre en el palmarés de esta distinción. La influencia de MARCA, y esto no es una afirmación presuntuosa ni orgullo de director sino un hecho meramente objetivo, ahí queda también para siempre. No es casualidad tampoco que apenas unos días antes el delantero británico luciera pletórico el trofeo que le acreditaba como ganador de 'Los 100 de MARCA'. Un premio, éste, que cuenta con un prestigioso y amplísimo jurado y que, en apenas cuatro ediciones ya ha logrado un gran reconocimiento internacional. Nuestro galardón ha sido, como muchos intuíamos, la antesala o el anticipo de lo vivido ayer en Londres. Para mí, ver cómo Kane ganaba 'Los 100' le restó mucho suspense a la gala de anoche. La experiencia es una aniquiladores de sorpresas. Pero ya todo es historia. Queda abierta la carrera para los premios 2027.

articles.title: 'Streets ahead of everyone else!' - Paul Scholes tells Man Utd to ignore 'madman' warning and appoint Antonio Conte
articles.summary: Paul Scholes believes Antonio Conte is the only viable candidate to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The club legend insists the volatile Italia...
articles.body:
Paul Scholes believes Antonio Conte is the only viable candidate to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The club legend insists the volatile Italian is the perfect manager to shake up the struggling squad and return them to Premier League contention.

Carrick is facing an increasingly uncertain future at United after a disastrous start to the campaign. The club has endured a dismal run of form, culminating in a heavy 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. That result leaves United with just one victory in their last eight Premier League outings.

Unfortunately for Carrick, the awful performances on the pitch have been matched by growing unrest behind the scenes. Lisandro Martinez has reportedly spoken out against the club's hierarchy . Meanwhile, club captain Bruno Fernandes has openly aimed criticism at Carrick and his coaching staff , highlighting a deeply fractured dressing room.

Scholes identifies the perfect replacement

If the club ultimately decides to make a managerial change, Scholes believes Conte is the ideal candidate . When presented with a shortlist including Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, the United legend was clear on his preference. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast , Scholes admitted the Italian would be a risky but necessary appointment to salvage the season.

"You'd have to pick a manager who you think will get us back to being a competitive team for the Premier League," Scholes explained. "Out of them three, Antonio Conte's the man, but he comes with a big f***ing massive warning.

"He's made noises that he wants to come and I'm pretty sure the club would have spoke to all three of them. I can't understand why he'd want this job because I don't think the team's good enough for him, personally.

Emery considered but Conte remains the priority

Scholes also suggested Aston Villa manager Unai Emery as a potential solution. He praised the Spaniard for consistently producing excellent results and winning the Europa League, despite frequently losing his best players to transfers. However, the United legend still views Conte as the superior option due to his elite pedigree.

"I think Conte's the best one around," Scholes noted. "When I'm talking best in class and you talk them four, I think Antonio Conte's miles ahead of all of them. You think Juventus, he went to Napoli and goes and wins the league with them. He's volatile, I know he's volatile and might be a bit of a madman, but when you talk about successful managers at top clubs he's streets ahead.

"I don't care if it's short term. I don't care if he's there 18 months and he gets us challenging for the league, that would be a success. The more and more I think about it, Conte needs to come in and start banging some heads together."

United must quickly shift their focus back to on-pitch matters as a demanding fixture awaits. They will face Chelsea in the Premier League on Saturday, and the pressure will intensify on Carrick if the squad fails to secure a victory.

articles.title: France Football chief reveals how close Kylian Mbappe came to winning 2026 Ballon d’Or: ‘Was leading for a long time’

articles.body:
Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe enjoyed an extraordinary 2025-26 campaign, scoring 42 goals for his club and another ten at the World Cup.

His performances made him one of the leading contenders for the Ballon d'Or, but it eventually went to Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane .

As quoted by AS , France Football editor-in-chief Vincent Garcia has now revealed just how close Mbappe came to winning his first-ever Ballon d'Or.

In fact, he confirmed that the Real Madrid superstar was leading the voting for a considerable period.

Mbappe was leading the Ballon d'Or voting

Speaking to L'Equipe after Monday's ceremony, Garcia confirmed that the battle between Kane and Mbappe was exceptionally close.

"The difference was even smaller than between Rodri and Vinicius in 2024, which was 41 points, and that was already a very narrow margin," he explained.

He also explained how Harry Kane overtook him at the last moment.

"Mbappe was leading for a long time, but Kane ended up winning. Mbappe has had an extraordinary season. It was incredibly close between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe in the battle for first place this year," he said.

Harry Kane pipped Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d'Or. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Garcia also suggested that Spain's World Cup success worked against individual candidates, with Rodri and Lamine Yamal splitting votes.

The Barcelona youngster eventually finished third, while his team-mate came fourth. For the longest time, it looked like Lamine was in the running for the award.

However, judging by Garcia's words, it looks like it was a two-horse race between Kane and Mbappe, with the former edging it.

Real Madrid star has every reason to remain optimistic

Mbappe's individual campaign brought him so close to winning the award even without winning a single trophy for club or country.

The French superstar would have almost certainly walked away with the award if Los Blancos had picked up at least one piece of silverware last summer.

Mbappe has started the new season in excellent form. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Ultimately, Kane's 73 goals for club and country, along with Bayern's domestic trophies, gave the Englishman an advantage.

Mbappe has already started the new season in excellent form, maintaining his ridiculously high goalscoring numbers.

He scored twice in Sunday's 2-1 Clasico victory over Barcelona. Mbappe will know that if he has another good campaign, he could take the final step towards the trophy next year.

At 27, the France international is in the prime of his career. His narrow Ballon d'Or defeat might be a bitter pill to swallow, but there will be future chances.

Turning his individual excellence into collective trophies will have to be the next step, and it remains to be seen how he fares for Madrid.

Ballon d'Or hangover? Hang in there a little longer, because last night's ceremony has left us with a few more interesting talking points.

🤔 A little dig from Harry Kane at his rivals?

"Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise. 🏆," Harry Kane wrote on social media after winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

The message, which looked very much like it had been carefully thought out and prepared in advance, sounds like a thinly veiled dig at Mbappé and Lamine Yamal, who have not hesitated to stake their claim to the award whenever they have had the chance.

📊 The closest Ballon d'Or race in history

"The race between Kane and Mbappé was incredibly tight. The gap was even smaller than the 41 points between Rodri and Vinicius in 2024, and that was already a very narrow margin. Mbappé led for a long time, but Kane ultimately came out on top," explains Vincent García, editor-in-chief of France Football.

Plenty of people on X have joked that Harry Kane is also the first goalkeeper to win the Ballon d'Or since Lev Yashin in 1963.

It all goes back to that Tottenham–Asteras Tripolis Europa League match in 2004, when he had to put on the gloves after Lloris was injured.

Let's not forget that Harry Kane is the only Ballon d'Or winner in the last 30 years never to have won an international trophy with either his national team or any of his clubs.

articles.title: Major Chinese brands drop Mbappé as backlash grows over Mao joke
articles.summary: He allegedly said his "favourite meme" is "the one where they put my face on a Chinese dictator".
articles.body:
Several Chinese brands have dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé as backlash grew online over alleged comments by him referring to the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Mbappé reportedly told French talk show The Bridge a meme "that makes me laugh the most...the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator". As he speaks, a meme appears with his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

"I use it with my friends all the time," the Real Madrid forward adds, in unverified clips that have been circulating online.

Mbappé does not identify Mao by name and the original video is no longer on the show's YouTube channel, but screengrabs have spread on Chinese social media.

Even China's foreign ministry has weighed in, with spokesperso Lin Jian: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

Neither Mbappé nor the The Bridge have commented on this yet.

It's unclear when the interview was broadcast but Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments on Monday night in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

A backlash quickly ensued online, with some users criticising Mbappé – who is very popular in China and has huge brand endorsements – of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public".

"International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," read another comment on Weibo.

Mao founded Communist China in 1949 and ruled through tumultuous decades in the 1960s and 1970s. His attempt at rapid industrialisation, which he called the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party.

His death in 1976 brought a new era for China, which began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao's rule, he continued to be hailed by the Chinese Communist Party as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach.

The backlash against Mbappé is still growing. Chinese state broadcaster, CCTV, is suspending La Liga matches, according to The Paper.

According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, CCTV's news apps no longer have content related to the French striker.

The Chinese brands have not explicitly said why they were terminating the contract but referred to hurt sentiments.

The country's largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people".

Drinks giant Dongpeng, said: "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments."

Given brands have not mentioned the controversial clip, some users on social media are also asking what exactly Mbappé had said or done that was offensive.

Mbappé, who made his debut for Real Madrid in August 2024, has been nicknamed "the dictator" in the football world because of his influence and control over club and international football operations.

In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop's sandwiches. Some say the incident reinforced his "dictator" portrayal.

The nickname has also made Mbappé the subject of many memes online.

France team-mate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup by calling Mbappé Mobut – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades.

In an interview with France Football in September, Mbappé acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they "sometimes reveals a lack of political and human awareness among people".

"There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history.

"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life," he had said.
